text:
Kim: Heads-up from a design pass — when the inline table action menu is open and a toast appears the menu gets clipped by the toast on small windows. Seen on 1366x768 and smaller. Screenshot: https://placeholder.img/table-menu-clipped.png
Omar: repro. The toast sits above the table layer currently, which is fine for alerts but bad for dropdowns that expect to be topmost.
Jules: This is also causing a subtle keyboard issue: users tabbing through the action menu sometimes move focus behind the toast and can't see where they are. a11y concern.
Kim: Ideas: 1) introduce a dedicated UI layer ordering doc (z-index map) so components know stack precedence, 2) keep toasts centered and non-obstructive for interactive elements, 3) ensure menus and modals always have higher stacking context than toasts.
Tara: I sketched a z-order convention: base < content < tooltips < toasts < menus < modals < overlays. That way menus sit above toasts. But we should be careful because toasts are often attached to document root and menus are inside relative parents which can create new stacking contexts.
Omar: CSS approach for toasts to avoid capturing clicks and focus:
```css
.red-toast { position: fixed; top: 16px; left: 50%; transform: translateX(-50%); z-index: var(--z-toast, 800); pointer-events: none; }
.red-toast:hover { pointer-events: auto; }
.table-menu { position: relative; z-index: var(--z-menu, 900); }
```
Jules: pointer-events none helps, but if menu is inside a container with transform or z-index it might still be under the toast. We should prefer menu creation at body level (portal) for any floating interactive component.
Kim: Agree. component guideline: floating interactive controls (menus, popovers, dropdowns) must portal to global layer. Add that to component docs.
Tara: Copy nit: toast copy uses "Saved" in some table rows and "Update complete" elsewhere. Suggest consistent tone: prefer concise verbs like "Saved" for inline row changes and "Updates saved" for bulk operations. We should add these to the content guidelines.
Omar: Focus visuals: icon-only table action buttons have a faint focus halo in dark mode. Recommend using the same focus token --focus-ring-2 with color token --color-focus-inverse for dark surfaces and ensure outline-offset: 3px so it doesn't overlap with row hover.
Jules: also add live region aria-assertions: toasts should announce succinctly but not disrupt screen reader focus. Use aria-live=polite for non-critical toasts and assert that opening a menu moves focus into the menu.
Kim: QA asks for an e2e: open action menu, trigger a toast, assert menu is still visible and activeElement is inside menu, verify no horizontal/vertical shift > 4px.
Tara: For spacing tokens — the table row action group uses --space-1 (4px) which feels cramped when there are 3 icons. Suggest a local override --row-action-gap: 8px for the component rather than changing the global token. We'll add a token in tokens.yml but not swap the global mapping yet.
Omar: I'll draft a small PR: 1) docs for z-index ordering and portal rules, 2) toast layer update to pointer-events none + transform entrance, 3) table actions portal + local spacing token, 4) focus ring dark-mode tweak, 5) copy harmonization.
Jules: Will run accessibility checks (NVDA/VoiceOver) and keyboard nav once PR is up. Also will sample with high-contrast mode on windows.
Kim: design-bot: can you open a tracking PR?
design-bot: PR opened: redwood/design-system#734 — "floating layers: toasts vs menus, table action spacing & focus" (assigned to Omar)
Tara: Thanks team. tagging @eng-runtime so they know not to hardcode toast z-index in infra embeds.
Omar: will include a brief note in DESIGN_TOKENS.md about ordering and show example values. ETA for PR: today EOD.
Kim: Awesome. Please link PR here when ready and include screenshots and the small E2E snippet so QA can verify quickly. :thumbsup:
